text: oil ob- tained from the fresh livers of Gadus morrhua and other species of Gadidae. It contains not less than 600 units (180 micrograms) and not more than 2500 units (750 micrograms) of vitamin A per g and not less than 60 units (1.5 micrograms) and not more than 250 units (6.25 micrograms) of vitamin D per g. It may be fla- voured by the addition of not more than 1% of a suitable flavour or a mixture of flavours. A suitable antoxidant may be added. A thin, oily liquid, having a characteristic, slightly fishy but not rancid odour. Slightly soluble in alcohol; freely soluble in carbon disulfide, in chloroform, in ether, and in ethyl acetate. Store in airtight containers. It may be bottled or packaged in containers from which air has been expelled by the production of a vacuum or by an inert gas. Profile Cod-liver oil is a rich source of vitamin D (p.1986) and a good source of vitamin A (p.1971). It also contains several essential fatty acids. Cod-liver oil dressings or ointment have been advocated to ac- celerate healing in burns, ulcers, pressure sores, and superficial wounds, but controlled observations have failed to substantiate claims of their value. Preparations USP 31: Cod Liver Oil Capsules.
